title: [Security] caclmgrd always allows all control plane traffic sourced from port TCP/179
author: bluecmd
body:
#### Description

I detected that all traffic that uses a source port TCP/179 will be allowed with no option of disabling this.

An attacker can trivially send packets with any source port they wish, so this would allow bypassing any control plane ACL.

#### Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Use SONiC and **optionally** apply control plane ACLs (even with or without control plane ACLs this exploit is possible)

#### Describe the results you received:

One of the first (i.e. highest priority) rules installed into iptables by caclmgrd is `iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --sport 179 -j ACCEPT` and `ip6tables -A INPUT -p tcp --sport 179 -j ACCEPT`.

Since source port is fully controllable by the client establishing the connection, hitting this rule is trivial. Since this rule is one of the highest priority rules (higher than block IP2ME and custom control plane ACLs) it is impossible to configure SONiC to not allow this traffic.

#### Describe the results you expected:

Control plane traffic should not judge traffic based on source port. Leave it to conntrack.

#### Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):

Example exploitation of an otherwise locked down IP2ME loopback address.

```
sudo nmap -g 179 -sS 11.11.11.111
Starting Nmap 7.70 ( https://nmap.org ) at 2022-01-27 20:22 UTC
Nmap scan report for 11.11.11.111
Host is up (0.000064s latency).
Not shown: 996 closed ports
PORT     STATE SERVICE
22/tcp   open  ssh
179/tcp  open  bgp
443/tcp  open  https
8080/tcp open  http-proxy

Nmap done: 1 IP address (1 host up) scanned in 14.91 seconds
```

Full disclosure: I filed this issue to help my PR fixing this #9827 move forward.

linkedPullRequests.title: [Security] caclmgrd: remove permit source port 179
linkedPullRequests.author: bluecmd
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

Fixes #9916.

I detected that all traffic that uses a source port TCP/179 will be allowed with no option of disabling this.

An attacker can trivially send packets with any source port they wish, so this would allow bypassing any control plane ACL.

#### How I did it

I removed these statements. They appear to be for allowing BGP, but the needed rules are already present:

 - Allow destination port 179
 - Allow established connections

#### How to verify it

If this patch is wrong BGP would not work, so test BGP and see that it works.
Also, you can check in a running instance /without/ this patch that `iptables -vnL` shows that 0 packets have been accepted into the `tcp spt:179` rule.

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)

- [ ] 201811
- [ ] 201911
- [ ] 202006
- [x] 202012
- [x] 202106
- [x] 202111

Reason: Security patch. caclmgrd was introduced in 202012 it seems.

#### Description for the changelog

caclmgrd: Remove explicit permit source port 179

comments.body:
I managed to create an easy repro. With a loopback interface configured as `11.11.11.111/32` a normal `nmap -sT 11.11.11.111` hits the DROP rule `  224 11200 DROP       all  --  *      *       0.0.0.0/0            11.11.11.111`. Scan takes very long time and no results.

However, using `sudo nmap -g 179 -sS 11.11.11.111` allows one to bypass all control plane ACLs:
